articles.title: ‘Your father is waiting’: How 8-year-old lured KG girl into empty classroom before brutal attack in Panchkula; staff remained unaware until parents arrive
articles.summary: PANCHKULA: An eight-year-old boy lured a six-year-old kindergarten girl into an empty classroom at a government school in Panchkula on October 28, telling
articles.body: PANCHKULA: An eight-year-old boy lured a six-year-old kindergarten girl into an empty classroom at a government school in Panchkula on October 28, telling her that her father was waiting there, before launching a brutal assault on her, CCTV footage shows.The boy allegedly kicked and punched the girl and banged her head against desks. The assault continued even after she lost consciousness, according to the footage.The circumstances that led to the attack remain unclear, and police are investigating the possible motive.The incident went unnoticed by school staff. It was only after the girl's parents learnt that she was missing from her usual pickup point that they rushed to the school and began searching for her. The girl was eventually found injured inside the premises.The disturbing CCTV footage has since circulated on social media, raising questions about the supervision of young children and the school's response to the incident.The girl is undergoing treatment at PGI-Chandigarh and is reported to be stable. Police have registered an FIR against the school principal and the class teacher.The eight-year-old boy was presented before the Juvenile Justice Board for psychological evaluation. A brain mapping test was conducted at PGI-Chandigarh on Saturday, with another round scheduled for Monday, sources said.Police are also examining whether exposure to online games or television content could have influenced the boy's behaviour. No trigger for the assault has been established so far.Teacher handling two classes with around 80 studentsA departmental inquiry into the incident has pointed to possible lapses in student supervision, with statements suggesting that a shortage of teachers had led to two classes being conducted together.According to sources, around 80 students from the two classes were being taught under the supervision of a single teacher.The class teacher told the inquiry committee that she was handling both classes on the day of the incident. She said the school had closed classes at around 3.15pm and that she had led the children in a line through a corridor towards the kitchen area as parents began arriving to collect them.The teacher later returned to the staff room, while a school attendant monitored the handover of children to their parents.Around 3.30pm, the autorickshaw driver who regularly ferried the girl informed her father that she was missing from the pickup point. Her family rushed to the school, triggering a search of the premises.The inquiry examined CCTV footage, statements from the boy and accounts given by parents and school employees.The Haryana State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has sought a detailed factual report, supporting documents and an action-taken report from the district education officer. The preliminary inquiry has been completed, and its findings are to be forwarded to the education directorate for consideration of further action over the alleged lapses.DCP Aditya Singh said mandatory standard operating procedures would be issued for schools, alongside sensitisation and outreach programmes.Attack raises concerns over aggression among childrenThe assault has prompted child psychologists and paediatricians to call for early intervention to address aggression among young children, with experts stressing the need to examine the circumstances surrounding the behaviour rather than assume a cause.Dr Adarsh Kohli, a clinical psychologist and former professor in PGI's department of psychiatry, said the boy's motives and psychological state needed to be examined. He also stressed the importance of extensive trauma counselling for the girl to address the risk of post-traumatic stress disorder and long-term difficulties with trust.Dr Bhavneet Bharti, a social paediatrician at PGI who works on adverse childhood experiences and the impact of social media on children, said an eight-year-old was still developing emotional regulation, impulse control and the ability to manage anger and frustration.She said an incident of such severity should not be dismissed as ordinary childhood fighting. Investigators and specialists needed to examine whether the child had experienced or witnessed violence, bullying, harsh punishment, emotional distress or other adverse childhood experiences.Bharti called on schools to introduce social-emotional learning from the primary years, helping children recognise anger, tolerate frustration, resolve conflicts and seek help before emotions escalate into aggression.Experts also highlighted the importance of examining children's exposure to violent media, unsupervised screen time and domestic conflict, while avoiding assumptions about what caused the attack.The incident has brought renewed attention to the need for closer supervision in schools, early identification of behavioural concerns and psychological support for children affected by violence.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: Sheetal Devi: Born without arms, she learned to shoot with her feet and became a world champion, Paralympic medallist and double gold winner at the 2026 Asian Para Games
articles.summary: A bow is usually held with one hand and drawn with the other. For Sheetal Devi, neither of those movements was an option.
articles.body: A bow is usually held with one hand and drawn with the other. For Sheetal Devi, neither of those movements was an option. Born without arms, the young archer from Jammu and Kashmir had to find a way to make the equipment work with the body she had. Her answer was a technique that is now recognised around the world. She steadies the bow with her foot, uses her shoulder to draw the string and releases the arrow with the help of her mouth. It is a demanding combination of balance, strength and control. And it has taken years of practice to perfect.Today, Devi is a Paralympic bronze medallist, a world champion and one of India's most celebrated para-archers. At the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, she added another major achievement to her record, winning two gold medals and a silver. But the medals tell only part of the story. Her journey is also about learning a skill in an entirely different way, accepting setbacks and continuing to improve.From everyday tasks to an unexpected sporting opportunityBorn on January 10, 2007, in Kishtwar district of Jammu and Kashmir, Sheetal grew up in the village of Loidhar. She learnt to perform everyday activities, including writing and eating, using her feet. These early experiences helped her develop the balance and control that would later become important in archery. Her sporting journey began to take shape after she was noticed at an Indian Army camp in 2019. The Army recognised her potential and helped her access educational and medical support. She eventually joined the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board Sports Complex in Katra, where she was introduced to sports.Coach Kuldeep Vedwan played an important role in guiding her towards para-archery. The sport was not an obvious choice, given that conventional archery depends heavily on the use of both arms. Yet her coach and the training team worked with her to explore a method that suited her abilities.At first, even lifting and controlling the bow was difficult. She had to build strength and learn how to coordinate different parts of her body. Training included resistance-band exercises, strength work and shooting at targets placed only a few metres away. With time, she developed the balance and control required to shoot at the standard competition distance of 50 metres. The process was gradual. Each practice session helped her understand what worked, what needed to change and how to make her movements more consistent.A technique built through patience and practiceSheetal's shooting style attracts attention because it looks very different from conventional archery. However, the technique is not a shortcut. It requires precise positioning, strong leg muscles, a stable body and careful control over every movement. She holds the bow with her foot and uses her shoulder to pull the string. A release aid held in her mouth helps her release the arrow. The sequence must be repeated with accuracy, even when the weather, wind or competition pressure makes shooting more difficult.Her progress soon began to show in international competitions. At the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, she won gold in the women's individual compound event and the mixed team event, along with a silver medal in women's doubles. She also won silver at the 2023 World Archery Para Championships. The next major milestone came at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games. Partnering with Rakesh Kumar, she won bronze in the mixed team compound event. At 17, she became India's youngest Paralympic medallist. Although she missed an individual podium finish in Paris, the experience became another stage in her development.In an interview with World Archery in October 2025, after winning the individual world title in Gwangju, South Korea, Sheetal spoke about the doubts she had faced. "I never paid attention to them; I just stayed focused on my game," she said. She also spoke about how rewarding it was to see young girls from distant places express an interest in taking up archery after watching her.Two gold medals, one silver and a bigger messageSheetal returned to the Asian Para Games in 2026 with the aim of defending the titles she had won in Hangzhou. She delivered two gold-medal performances in Japan, retaining the women's individual compound title and winning the compound mixed team event with Toman Kumar. She also earned silver in women's doubles with Payal Nag, completing a three-medal campaign.Speaking to the Asian Paralympic Committee after the victories, she said, "I'm very happy – two gold medals and a silver in my second Asian Para Games. It feels all the hard work done in the past years was rewarded in one day. She also explained how she approached the pressure of the final: "I was just thinking to shoot my best; follow the process." It was a simple description of the focus that has shaped her career.Her story has reached people well beyond the archery field. In a 2024 interview with World Archery, Sheetal spoke about receiving messages from children with disabilities who wanted to follow her example. She said she hoped more people would believe they could achieve something despite their disabilities. She also urged parents to support their children and recognise what they are capable of.Sheetal shares updates through her Instagram account, @sheetal_archery. The belief, along with the training and support she has received, has helped her build a career on her own terms. Her achievements are not simply a story of winning despite a physical condition. articles.title: Donald Trump speaks to Benjamin Netanyahu as US weighs fresh military strikes on Iran: Report
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu by telephone on Saturday as Washington assessed options for potentially
articles.body: US President Donald Trump spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu by telephone on Saturday as Washington assessed options for potentially resuming military operations against Iran, according to a US media report citing people familiar with the conversation.The call followed a meeting at the White House earlier in the week, during which Trump discussed possible military action with senior military commanders, The Wall Street Journal reported.The diplomatic engagement comes as the US continues to explore negotiations with Tehran while keeping the possibility of fresh military strikes open. US secretary of state Marco Rubio said talks with Iran had not stopped, adding that Trump had yet to decide whether to resume military action.Speaking to reporters after the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Georgia, Rubio said Washington remained open to a diplomatic settlement, provided it addressed US security concerns.“There are multiple talks; talks have actually never stopped. There's been active conversations going both in some cases directly, but often through intermediaries,” he said.Asked how long the US would allow diplomatic efforts to continue before considering military action, Rubio declined to set a deadline or assess the progress of negotiations.“I'm not gonna characterise either the progress on those talks or any timeframe on it other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it,” he said.Rubio said any agreement would have to address Iran's nuclear programme and its support for armed groups in the region. He also accused Tehran of threatening commercial shipping and disrupting maritime trade.On the possibility of renewed strikes, the US secretary of state declined to discuss specific military plans but said Washington believed it could achieve its objectives through force if required.“We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. He hasn't made a decision,” Rubio said, referring to Trump.US, Israel reportedly prepare for possible escalationThe Jerusalem Post, citing Israeli defence assessments, reported that the US and Israel were preparing for the possibility of renewed strikes, although Israeli officials remained uncertain about the timing of any escalation.According to the report, Israeli defence officials believe Iran is unlikely to accept an agreement requiring it to completely abandon its nuclear programme or stop producing ballistic missiles.They also assess that Tehran may be seeking to prolong negotiations ahead of the US midterm elections.The report said that despite preparations by the US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) for a possible operation, the White House was not expected to order strikes before the midterm elections unless it detected preparations for a surprise attack.The US and Israel have reportedly also drawn up plans for renewed strikes after the elections.The Jerusalem Post further reported that more than 3,000 American troops were stationed in Israel, while there had been no sharp increase in the number of US military aircraft redirected to the country during the previous week.Last week, 10 US Air Force transport aircraft arrived at Israeli Air Force bases in southern Israel as part of a wider military air convoy moving equipment across the Middle East, according to KAN News.The aircraft had travelled from Fort Bliss in Texas and were believed to be carrying air defence systems.Other aircraft in the convoy landed in Jordan, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. The report also referred to the transfer of an additional Patriot air defence system to the region.Iran signals response to US diplomatic overtureEven as Washington continued to signal its willingness to negotiate, Iranian officials offered their assessment of the latest diplomatic exchanges.Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said the tone of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance had changed significantly.“Their tone has shifted completely, which is a good sign that shows that our people have secured their victory,” Rezaei told Iranian state broadcaster IRIB.The letter was delivered to Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, through Qatari mediators on Sunday. According to The New York Times, the US proposal envisaged direct talks led by Vance, with Iran's nuclear programme included in discussions from the outset.The Wall Street Journal, citing a source, reported that the communication outlined a “framework for negotiations” rather than specific peace terms. The letter was sent at Trump's direction.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran had studied the letter and described Washington's attempt to initiate dialogue as a “positive step”. He also said an aide had travelled to Doha for consultations with mediators.Citing sources, Al Jazeera reported that a meeting could take place within a week, with Doha and Istanbul being considered as possible venues.Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, meanwhile, warned that the country's armed forces would respond to any military or terrorist attacks by the US or Israel.He said Iran's response would be “geographically unrestricted”, adding that the armed forces and the Iranian people would determine the timing and conditions for ending any future confrontation.Rubio accuses Tehran of threatening maritime tradeRubio also criticised Iran's conduct at sea, accusing Tehran of deliberately targeting commercial vessels carrying cargo, oil and natural gas.He said US naval forces were intercepting incoming drones and anti-ship missiles almost every night. Despite the security concerns, he said petroleum transit volumes remained comparable to pre-conflict levels.The secretary of state warned that disruptions to maritime trade could have consequences for global food security, particularly if supplies of fuel, agricultural inputs and food commodities were affected.He also accused Iran of supporting armed groups across the Middle East, including Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis and militias challenging the Iraqi state.“So anywhere you turn, what you find is some Iranian proxy that's undermining the peace and stability of the Middle East,” Rubio said.Trump had said at the White House on Friday that Tehran was keen to negotiate, reiterating that diplomatic contacts were under way.“There are talks, they want to talk, they keep talking,” he said, adding, “We have time, frankly.”The US president also claimed Iran was “in a lot of trouble” and predicted that the conflict would end “very soon”.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ancient Romans put warning signs outside their homes too; what the famous 'beware of the dog' mosaic in Pompeii tells us about everyday life
articles.summary: For those of us who are fearful of dogs, we take a moment before entering a house with a “Beware of the Dog!” sign.
articles.body: For those of us who are fearful of dogs, we take a moment before entering a house with a “Beware of the Dog!” sign. While it serves as a warning, the sign has a 2,000-year-old history, and its roots can be traced to the ancient Roman world. Variations of these signs can be seen all around the world today, but the story behind them deserves a moment of its own.In the Roman city of Pompeii, the Latin phrase “CAVE CANEM” has been greeting visitors for a long time, yet not everyone knows what it means.What is “CAVE CANEM”?Believe it or not, the sign reading “Beware of the Dog” is not a modern discovery. It is not a result of modern civilisation and its love for dogs. Ancient Romans had a mosaic depicting a dog with a spiked collar, with the Latin phrase “CAVE CANEM” written beside it. The phrase translates to “Beware of the Dog”, but its meaning is not that simple. The dog in the famous Roman mosaic is neither sitting nor standing; rather, it is lunging forward, ready to pounce. It is not just a warning against dogs, but an intimidating dog mosaic placed at the vestibulum to scare off thieves and trespassers.The mosaic was discovered during excavations in 1824–1825 in the House of the Tragic Poet in the Roman city of Pompeii, Regio VI, Insula 8. Even though the house was not among the largest residences in Pompeii, it was exceptional in its appearance. Walls painted with frescoes, high-quality mosaic designs and scenes from Greek mythology adorned the house, along with this peculiar warning sign. The sign served multiple purposes before the house was buried by the volcanic eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79.Why did Romans need these signs?The domestication of dogs is not a novel phenomenon of the modern world; it has been a centuries-old practice. The sign served a security function. Whenever anybody entered the house, they were made aware that a scary dog on a leash might be waiting for them if they entered with ill intentions. Describing the functions that dogs served for Romans, the poet Virgil wrote that “never with them on guard need you fear for your stalls a midnight thief, or onslaught of wolves.”Moreover, it was preferred that large, darker dogs were kept, as they were considered ideal for protecting the home. In the murals of Pompeii, a dark dog against a light background is also depicted. Darker dogs were considered intimidating during the day and less visible at night, making them suitable guards. Roman writer Columella described how black farmyard dogs could “terrify thieves in the daytime” and remain “less visible to trespassers at night.”Entrance was more than just a doorwayIn Roman homes, the entrance was considered an important space in the house, one that was carefully managed. It was the doorway from the public sphere to the private sphere of the family. This was the first space that a visitor encountered when entering. While some entrances offered warm greetings with phrases like Salve, meaning “welcome” or “be well”, others had an intimidating message of Cave Canem. It was believed to be the place where the house defined itself by providing the first message.Was it also an indication of social status?The sign served its obvious purpose of giving a warning, but it could also communicate wealth and taste. Such a sign was not cheap. It was crafted intricately using mosaics, suggesting an investment of time and money. Even though the House of the Tragic Poet was not the largest house, it had magnificent frescoes and mosaics, suggesting a certain degree of social standing.The first-century Roman work Satyricon, attributed to Petronius, describes a character encountering a painted dog and a Cave Canem inscription at a house entrance. The detail suggests that this kind of warning was familiar enough to feature in Roman literature, even as an object of satire.Perhaps the most fascinating thing about the Cave Canem mosaic is how little its message has changed over the centuries. In modern times, the materials may have changed from mosaic designs to printed boards and metal plaques, but the intention remains the same. It is to protect a home and warn those who want to enter it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Amit Shah to spearhead BJP’s UP outreach before state polls with 18-rally plan
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Days after pitching the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) as the BJP’s next major agenda item in Uttar Pradesh, Union home minister
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Days after pitching the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) as the BJP’s next major agenda item in Uttar Pradesh, Union home minister Amit Shah is set to lead an extensive statewide campaign, with the party planning rallies across all 18 divisions of the state as it begins preparations for the 2027 assembly elections.Party sources said Shah’s address at the BJP state working committee meeting in Lucknow on Friday was the first in a series of proposed engagements aimed at energising the organisation ahead of the electoral battle. He is also likely to be the chief guest at Ayodhya’s Deepotsav celebrations on November 7 and address a public gathering there.After Diwali, Shah is expected to address rallies in the remaining divisions, effectively covering all 18 administrative divisions of Uttar Pradesh.Senior BJP leaders said the exercise is aimed at galvanising booth-level workers and strengthening the party organisation well before the start of the election campaign.The BJP has also proposed at least 20 rallies by Prime Minister Narendra Modi across the state, with a minimum of three programmes in each of the party’s six organisational regions - Kashi, Gorakhpur, Awadh, Kanpur-Bundelkhand, Brij-Rohilkhand and West UP. The final schedule, however, is subject to approval from the Prime Minister’s Office, party leaders said.Addressing over 2,500 party workers at the state working committee meeting, Shah praised the Yogi Adityanath government for the robust law and order and development initiatives, and said a fresh BJP mandate would pave the way for implementation of the UCC in Uttar Pradesh. Drawing parallels with the abrogation of Article 370 and the construction of the Ram temple, he said the BJP had consistently delivered on its ideological commitments.Shah asserted that the BJP’s organisational strength made it a formidable force in the state. He also projected long-term political dominance for the party and urged workers to focus on strengthening the organisation at the grassroots.According to party sources, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath informed the meeting that an invitation had been extended to Shah to attend Deepotsav as chief guest, while BJP national general secretary and UP in-charge Vinod Tawde later told party functionaries that Shah would be addressing rallies across all divisions as part of the organisational mobilisation drive.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Two US senators write letter to Google CEO Sundar Pichai asking 9 questions as company pushes for AI in classrooms
articles.summary: Google wants AI in schools, but two US senators want answers from CEO Sundar Pichai first.
articles.body: Google wants AI in schools, but two US senators want answers from CEO Sundar Pichai first. Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley have written a letter seeking answers from the tech giant, following an investigation into how the company’s AI tools affect schoolchildren. In a letter sent to Pichai, the senators asked what the company knows about the impact of its AI products on children’s mental health and educational development. The senators asked 9 questions from Pichai, while highlighting that “Google is forcing their AI products into classrooms across America, and children are paying the price.” Senators have given November 2 as the deadline for the Search giant to respond.“We write with grave concern that Google’s aggressive push of A.I. products to children in schools is threatening the academic success and overall wellbeing of an entire generation. We write to request information about Google’s promotion of A.I. products in schools and details about the research it has conducted on potential harms to children’s educational and emotional development,” the senators wrote.They claimed that “Google’s push of AI in classrooms appears to have created negative consequences for many students.” Citing an article from Wall Street Journal in which the publication interviewed more than 60 teachers, parents, students and clinicians, the senators highlighted that “test scores on national have declined and many students are increasingly unable to think critically or complete assignments independently after AI was introduced to the classroom.”9 questions Senators asked Google CEO Sundar PichaiGoogle is forcing their A.I. products into classrooms across America, and children are paying the price. We cannot repeat the mistakes of social media platforms where products are pushed onto children putting profit ahead of young peoples’ best interest. In light of this concerning reporting, I request answers to the following questions by November 2nd, 2026:1. In at least one case, Google’s own researchers warned the company about children’s AI usage. What research has Google conducted on the potential of Gemini, AI Overviews AI Mode, and other AI products to cause negative impacts on children’s mental wellbeing? Please provide this research.2. Why has Google set A.I. product integration as the default and, in some cases, made it impossible to disable these features on licensed education devices?3. Have school districts, teachers, or parents raised concerns with Google over children’s academic or emotional reliance on AI? Please describe any record of these concerns and Google’s responses.4. What support has Google provided to school districts who have raised concerns about Google’s AI products negatively impacting students?5. Please describe all promotional programs or offerings from Google that expand AI adoption in schools, including how much money Google has spent on these programs.6. Please share any resources Google has provided to school districts, administrators, and teachers adopting Google’s AI tools, in particular material addressing appropriate use and protecting students’ wellbeing.7. Has Google identified occurrences in which its classroom AI tools encouraged a minor to engage in harmful behavior, emotional dependence, or failed to detect signs of suicidal or self-harm ideation?8. After the publication of a research paper by Google researchers titled “The Ethics of Advanced AI Assistants,” what steps did Google take in response to its findings to limit harmful effects of AI for children?9. Google has stated that it has prioritized youth protections, particularly around emotional dependence and reinforcement of false beliefs. Please describe what steps Google has taken to prevent their A.I. chatbots from engaging in sycophantic or emotional conversations with children, including in light of failures to protect the Maryland student who was hospitalized after developing an intense dependence on Google’s AI.You use AI every day. articles.title: Six Indian tourists go missing during trek to Nepal's Shey-Phoksundo Lake
articles.summary: Six Indian tourists, including two women and four men, have gone missing during a trek to Nepal's Shey-Phoksundo Lake, the deepest lake in the country,
articles.body: Six Indian tourists, including two women and four men, have gone missing during a trek to Nepal's Shey-Phoksundo Lake, the deepest lake in the country, following heavy snowfall in the Himalayan region, officials confirmed to news agency ANI.The tourists were travelling from Ward Nos. 4 and 8 of Dolpo Buddha Rural Municipality towards the lake when they went missing. They were last reported to be in the Numla Pass and Bagla Pass areas between Ward Nos. 4 and 8 of Shey-Phoksundo Rural Municipality.Local guides suspect that the tourists may have become stranded in the mountains following heavy snowfall, reportedly influenced by Cyclone Arnab developing over the Bay of Bengal.According to local officials, the group continued its journey despite warnings from residents about difficult weather and dangerous conditions along the mountain passes. They are believed to have become trapped in the snow while returning from the high-altitude area.Dolpa chief district officer Junu Hamal confirmed that the tourists were stranded while returning from Dho towards Phoksundo Lake."The tourists became stranded while returning from Dho towards Phoksundo Lake," Hamal said, adding that locals had warned them about the difficult weather and mountain conditions before they proceeded.Shey-Phoksundo Rural Municipality Chairman Dhawa Samduk Gurung said the lack of mobile phone connectivity in the mountain passes had made it difficult to establish contact with the missing tourists."Mobile phone communication is unavailable in the mountain passes between Wards 4 and 8, making it difficult to obtain information about the tourists' whereabouts and current condition," Gurung said.Search and rescue ops under wayAuthorities have initiated efforts to trace the missing tourists, but heavy snowfall and adverse weather conditions have hampered search and rescue operations in the high-altitude region.Dolpa deputy superintendent of police Anil Raj Giri said the six Indian tourists remained uncontactable as per the latest information."Six Indian tourists remain out of contact, according to the latest information," Giri said.He added that authorities had requested the concerned agency to arrange a helicopter to assist in search and rescue operations.A team of the Nepal army has also been deployed to locate the tourists and help with the rescue efforts.The absence of mobile connectivity, thick snow and difficult terrain have made it challenging for rescue teams to establish the group's exact location and assess their condition.Over 240 tourists in Upper DolpaAccording to the District Administration Office, 244 tourists have reached Upper Dolpa. They include 149 Nepali nationals, 44 tourists from SAARC countries and 51 visitors from other foreign countries.Amid the worsening weather conditions, the district administration has urged tourists to avoid risky areas and remain in safe locations.Tourist arrivals in the Shey-Phoksundo Lake region have increased in recent years. Official data show that 4,882 tourists visited Phoksundo Lake during the first 11 months of the fiscal year 2082/83.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Former Metropolitan Police employee forged medical certificates to claim around 200 days of sick leave over two years, costing the force nearly £19,000 before she admitted fraud in court
articles.summary: A former Metropolitan Police employee admitted forging medical certificates to justify around 200 days of absence from work over nearly two years.
articles.body: A former Metropolitan Police employee admitted forging medical certificates to justify around 200 days of absence from work over nearly two years. Natasha Fountain, 29, pleaded guilty to fraud by misrepresentation at Westminster Magistrates’ Court after submitting falsified sick notes to her line manager between November 4, 2022, and May 3, 2024. The scheme cost the Metropolitan Police approximately £19,000, according to the court. Fountain had worked as a communications and engagement officer for the force between June 2022 and August 2024. HR Grapevine reported that her initial sickness absence was supported by a genuine medical certificate before she began submitting forged documents.Natasha Fountain submitted forged sick notes over nearly two yearsFountain, a former communications and engagement officer at the Metropolitan Police, submitted fraudulent medical certificates to justify extended periods away from work. According to HR Grapevine, she worked for the force from June 2022 until August 2024. Although her first sickness absence was supported by a legitimate medical note, she subsequently submitted forged documents between November 4, 2022, and May 3, 2024. These certificates enabled her to claim approximately 200 days of sick leave. Fountain, who appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court by video link in March 2026, admitted committing fraud by misrepresentation.Fake medical certificates cost the Metropolitan Police nearly £20,000The fraudulent sick notes resulted in an estimated £19,000 cost to the Metropolitan Police, the court heard. Prosecutors raised concerns about the authenticity of the documents, including inconsistencies involving the GP practice that supposedly issued them. There was no record of appointments between Fountain and her GP practice during the relevant dates. The practice had also changed its address, but the correspondence presented by Fountain did not reflect that change. These discrepancies formed part of the evidence surrounding the forged medical certificates. HR Grapevine reported that the documents had been used to justify her prolonged absence from the force.Court hears former Met employee had physical and mental health difficultiesThe court also heard that Fountain had experienced physical and mental health difficulties, including severe anxiety. Her condition reportedly prevented her from returning to her GP to obtain ongoing treatment and genuine medical certificates. District Judge Briony Clarke described the fraud as "quite sophisticated", explaining that Fountain had gone beyond simply lying by actively forging documents. The judge said further information was needed about Fountain's health during the period in question. She indicated that the court should examine whether genuine medical conditions had affected her ability to work, rather than considering the fraud without that context.Natasha Fountain admitted fraud and awaits sentencingFountain pleaded guilty to fraud by misrepresentation at Westminster Magistrates’ Court in March 2026. District Judge Briony Clarke delayed sentencing to allow further information about her health at the time of the offences to be gathered. The judge said that any genuine medical conditions affecting her ability to work could be relevant to the sentencing decision. Fountain was granted unconditional bail and was due to return to Westminster Magistrates’ Court on April 20, 2026, for sentencing, according to HR Grapevine's March 26 report. The report did not provide the outcome of that later hearing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Ahead of the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, the BJP released a poster titled \"Thago Ka Mela' (Fair of Thugs)\", targeting Congress
articles.body: Ahead of the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, the BJP released a poster titled "Thago Ka Mela' (Fair of Thugs)", targeting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition leaders.Designed in the style of a film poster, the graphic, released by BJP Delhi, features Rahul Gandhi, Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee and Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, among other INDIA bloc leaders.The poster accuses the opposition leaders of spreading rumours and creating anarchy in the country at the behest of anti-national forces to protect their political interests. Taking a swipe at the leaders, it carries the lines: "Directed by Rahul Gandhi and produced by Akhilesh Yadav."Sharing the poster on X, the BJP's Delhi unit wrote: "Today, at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, it's going to be held again - 'The Fair of Thugs'. Objective - To spread rumors and anarchy in the country at the behest of anti-national forces in order to save their political ground."INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila MaidanThe poster comes as opposition parties gather at Ramlila Maidan for the INDIA bloc's 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' rally, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the electoral process.Protesters from several states, including Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh, reached Delhi to participate in the demonstration. They raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod" and voiced concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the use of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), reported ANI.Some protesters from Punjab alleged that police barricades along the Punjab-Haryana border delayed their journey to Delhi, with several vehicles stranded overnight. They accused the BJP of trying to prevent people from attending the rally. These allegations have not been independently established.Protesters also demanded a return to ballot paper voting. Panna Lal Sharma, who travelled from Rajasthan, said he had joined the demonstration to oppose alleged electoral irregularities and demand the use of ballot papers.Uttarakhand Congress secretary Madanpal Singh said the protesters would continue their agitation until the Chief Election Commissioner resigned.The rally mobilisation havre also drawn participants from Himachal Pradesh, some of whom raised concerns over issues such as examination paper leaks, youth-related problems and alleged curbs on democratic rights.According to the rally schedule, INDIA bloc MPs were to assemble at the Constitution Club at 11 am before proceeding towards Ramlila Maidan from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction at noon.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: As thousands of people gathered at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday for the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ rally, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As thousands of people gathered at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday for the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ rally, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi urged participants to support local traders by shopping from their stores during the festive season. His appeal came after traders’ associations opposed the November 1 rally, warning that the gathering could disrupt business in the capital’s key commercial markets.In a video message posted on X late on Saturday, Gandhi appealed to people travelling to Delhi from different parts of the country to support small businesses by purchasing goods after attending the rally. He said the gathering would not hurt traders and accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of spreading rumours about its economic impact.“Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,” Gandhi said.“Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” he added.Reiterating his appeal, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha said: “I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours.”“But let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders,” he said, while extending Diwali greetings.Traders flag festive-season business lossesGandhi's appeal follows representations by the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) and the Federation of Sadar Bazar Traders Association, which had urged him and Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi to defer the November 1 rally until after the festive season.In its letter, CTI warned that an estimated 10 lakh participants and 15,000-20,000 vehicles could trigger severe traffic congestion across central Delhi's commercial markets.“We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown,” the traders' body said.The Federation of Sadar Bazar Traders Association also highlighted the financial stakes, stating that the period from Dhanteras to Diwali accounts for an estimated business turnover of around Rs 25,000 crore. It warned that disruption could affect shopkeepers, workers, delivery personnel and other people dependent on the festive trade.The association urged Rahul to take up the concerns of Delhi’s trading community with the Congress leadership and seek a postponement of the rally until after November 10, so businesses could complete their festive-season operations without disruption.The INDIA bloc rally, however, is being held at Ramlila Maidan against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Protesters gathering at the venue have raised slogans including “Vote chor, gaddi chhod”, demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Karnataka woman pays Rs 1.99 lakh to wedding photographer who promised personal coverage, finds assistants covering ceremonies instead; consumer court orders Rs 35,000 compensation and litigation expenses
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A wedding photographer in Karnataka has been directed to pay Rs 35,000 in compensation and litigation expenses to a bride after a consumer
articles.body: BENGALURU: A wedding photographer in Karnataka has been directed to pay Rs 35,000 in compensation and litigation expenses to a bride after a consumer court found deficiency in service over his failure to personally cover her wedding despite an alleged promise to do so, according to report by Bar and Bench.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Hassan held that replacing a specifically engaged photographer with assistants without informing the client or obtaining her consent amounted to a breach of contract under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.According to a report by Bar and Bench, the order was passed on October 17 by a bench comprising Commission president Chanchala CM and member Anupama R in a complaint filed by Chinmayi M against Karthik Singh, proprietor of Karthik Singh Photography and his associate Sharvari.Chinmayi had hired Singh after viewing his Instagram portfolio, which showcased his photography and videography work. The parties agreed on a package worth Rs 2.05 lakh, covering candid and cinematic videography for the engagement and other wedding-related ceremonies. She paid Rs 1,99,200, including Rs 16,200 towards travel expenses.According to the complaint, Singh had assured her that he would personally photograph important ceremonies, including the engagement, wedding reception and wedding. However, he allegedly sent other photographers without informing her.The bride alleged that the team arrived 70 minutes late and missed several important moments, including rituals at her home, the bridal procession accompanied by relatives and musicians, and the groom's arrival in a car.She further alleged that the photographers later asked the family to recreate some of the missed moments artificially.The complaint also raised concerns over poorly edited videos, missing footage, the absence of drone coverage, the placement of an LED screen and delays of nearly a year in delivering the photographs, videos and wedding album.Singh denied the allegations, maintaining that the photographers were part of his regular professional team and worked under his supervision. He argued that the complainant had failed to establish any technical deficiencies in the work and was attempting to avoid paying an outstanding amount of Rs 22,000.The Commission, however, found that Singh had failed to honour his commitment to personally photograph the ceremonies. It also observed that clients engage professionals based on their individual skills and expertise, making their identity an important consideration in such contracts."In professional contracts involving creative or specialized skills like photography, medical procedures, or legal representation the identity and unique talent of the service provider are often the primary reason for the contract. Substituting that person with an assistant without the client's consent constitutes a direct breach of contract," it said, as quoted by Bar and Bench.The Commission said photographers must inform clients if they are unable to attend an event, giving them an opportunity to make alternative arrangements.It relied on WhatsApp conversations to establish that the photographer's assistants had arrived 70 minutes late, resulting in important wedding rituals being missed.However, the Commission rejected the allegations concerning the poor quality of photographs and the absence of drone coverage.It directed Singh and his associate to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. articles.title: Meet Atiksh Bhan, the student who tested different incentives to reduce smartphone use during face-to-face conversations in a randomised trial
articles.summary: Smartphones are ubiquitous today in social interactions, frequently competing for attention even when people are sitting together.
articles.body: Smartphones are ubiquitous today in social interactions, frequently competing for attention even when people are sitting together. Student researcher Atiksh Bhan explored whether simple incentives could motivate people to put away their phones when talking face-to-face. His project, titled Designing for Presence, explored different ways of reducing smartphone use through a randomised trial. The research focused on how small changes in behaviour and the way people are encouraged can help make in-person interactions more attentive and meaningful.What did Atiksh Bhan investigate through his smartphone use studyAtiksh Bhan, a student from Manassas, Virginia, chose to examine a behaviour that has become familiar in homes, schools, restaurants and public spaces. Known as phubbing, it describes the habit of looking at or using a smartphone while interacting with someone in person. Rather than simply asking people to switch off their devices, Bhan investigated whether incentives could encourage them to give more attention to the people around them. His research brought together social behaviour, mental health and practical ways to encourage change.The project, titled ‘Designing for Presence: A Randomised Controlled Trial Comparing Incentive Structures to Reduce Smartphone Use During Social Interactions,’ examined how different forms of encouragement could influence phone use during conversations.According to the Society for Science, phubbing affects an estimated 75% of smartphone users. The behaviour has also been associated with depression, loneliness and dissatisfaction in relationships. These connections made the subject relevant beyond everyday phone etiquette, giving Bhan an opportunity to explore how technology habits can affect people's social experiences.How did the student conduct the researchBhan used a randomised controlled trial to study smartphone behaviour in real social settings. According to the Society for Science, the study involved 132 adults, of whom 62% were women.Instead of restricting the research to an artificial laboratory setting, he observed existing social groups in public spaces. The observation sessions lasted an average of 75 minutes, allowing him to examine phone-related behaviour during ordinary social interactions.The reason we randomised was because the project was about comparing different incentive structures, not about people’s opinions on their smartphone habits.Bhan might also study behaviour in groups, looking at how the presence and actions of other people could affect an individual’s willingness to put a phone away.Phubbing is an important social concernSmartphones make it easy to communicate, access information and stay connected. However, their constant availability can also interrupt conversations that take place in person.Phubbing describes precisely this situation. Even a brief interruption can change the experience of a conversation, particularly when one person feels that their attention is being divided.Instead of treating smartphone use as a habit that people must simply abandon, the project considered whether the surrounding social environment could help encourage different choices.This is an important distinction, because using your smartphone isn't always a conscious choice to ignore someone. They merely check their notifications because they are used to it or feel they should be available. Understanding these patterns can help researchers explore more practical ways to encourage attentive interactions.What did the trial reveal about changing phone habitsOne of the important observations from Bhan's research was that incentives alone might not explain why people change their behaviour. The Society for Science reported that the findings pointed towards the influence of interdependent group dynamics.In simple terms, the decisions people make about using their phones might be affected by what other people in their social group are doing. When people are in groups their behaviour can affect each other. This suggests that encouraging a whole group to remain engaged could be more effective than focusing exclusively on individual phone users.The research demonstrated a new approach known as contingency management, which uses incentives to encourage a desired behaviour. According to the Society for Science, the approach could be applied in cafeterias, at events and in other social environments where people gather.Atiksh Bhan was recognised at the 2026 science fairBhan's work received recognition at the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF), where he competed in the behavioural and social sciences category.According to the Society for Science, his project received the second award, worth $2,400. He represented Charles J. Colgan Sr. High School in Virginia and qualified through the Prince William-Manassas Regional Science and Engineering Fair.The competition brought together high school students who had earned their places by winning awards at affiliated local, regional, state or national science fairs. The 2026 edition was the 76th annual event.Bhan's project also appeared in the organisation's special awards announcement. The May 15 report listed him among the recipients of complimentary student affiliate memberships under the American Psychological Association's recognition programme.The research does not suggest that smartphones are inherently harmful or that every instance of checking a device damages a relationship. Smartphones are unlikely to disappear from everyday interactions, but the way people use them around others can influence the quality of those experiences.You use AI every day. articles.title: He sells peanuts till 3 am and makes it to class by 7:30: Meet Ariston Era III, the marine engineering student who works as a street vendor after class to pay his fees
articles.summary: When people say someone is working for peanuts, they don’t mean that positively, but this college student from the Philippines just proved them wrong.
articles.body: When people say someone is working for peanuts, they don’t mean that positively, but this college student from the Philippines just proved them wrong. While most college students look forward to returning home after a long day of classes, Ariston Era III has another responsibility waiting for him.A third-year Marine Engineering student at the University of the Visayas, Ariston spends his nights selling peanuts on the streets, sometimes continuing until 3 am. A time when most students are busy getting their lives together and figuring things out, he has built a routine around his studies, one that has helped him pay his own tuition fees, manage his daily expenses, and even help his family.A journey that began at the age of 11Ariston’s experience with selling began long before he entered college. During a conversational podcast with SunStar's Beyond the Headlines, he talked about his life journey. At just 11 years old, he started helping his mother sell homemade food such as embutido and empanadas within their neighbourhood in Bogo City. His mother, who had also sold goods and food while studying in college, became his biggest inspiration.His first independent venture was selling quail eggs, which he sourced from a neighbour. When that business stopped, he tried selling mangoes but soon realised that carrying them around was too tiring, eventually switching to peanuts, which were not only easier to transport and had a longer shelf life.What began as a way to earn some money gradually became part of his everyday life. However, Ariston says he does not see selling as something he does only because he has no other choice. For him, it is also about making productive use of his time and earning through honest work.Balancing marine engineering and selling peanutsHis schedule leaves little to no room for himself. After selling peanuts late into the night, Ariston wakes up at around 5 am, irons his uniform, prepares his stock and checks everything he needs to take to college, where he needs to be before 7:30 am before the commencement of classes, partly because some of his regular customers are fellow students who want to buy peanuts before classes.He has been taking full responsibility for his tuition and daily allowance since his second year. As the eldest of five siblings, he also wants to be in a position to help his family whenever they need financial support. His four younger siblings are still studying, and he says he is ready to contribute whenever his family is short of money.His parents were initially worried about him selling on the streets, particularly because he was living and studying in Cebu. He even kept the work from them at first, but they eventually came around and supported his decision to continue.His mother remains his biggest inspirationAriston’s mother has played an important role in shaping how he looks at work. Having seen her continue selling goods while pursuing her own education, he grew up understanding that earning a living through small businesses was nothing to be embarrassed about.He also does not want people to look down on him for selling peanuts. In his view, there is nothing shameful about doing honest work, and he would rather spend his time earning and helping hsi family than pretend to be someone he is not.For Ariston, the path is clear- to build a business that could be proudly his and though he hopes to see himself at the sea, marine Engineering, for him, is more of a way to raise the capital and build financial stability for his family.From selling peanuts to building a businessThat ambition is already taking shape. Ariston is currently working on setting up a local delivery service called Speedy Delivery in Bogo City. The idea is to handle everyday errands and deliveries, including food, groceries and medicines, across nearby areas. Some of his friends, who were previously unemployed, have joined the effort as delivery riders, while Ariston also takes on deliveries himself. The team is still working through the necessary paperwork.His plans go beyond delivery services, with interests in real estate and other businesses. He hopes that one day, if he becomes financially comfortable, he can build a shelter for stray animals, including dogs, cats and snakes, which he believes are often the most misunderstood and unfairly portrayed creatures.For now, however, his days continue to revolve around college, peanuts and the business he hopes to build. Ariston believes that people should not measure their progress against someone else's journey, and that having less money does not mean having no hope or ambition. For a student who has spent years balancing his education with work, that belief is reflected in the choices he continues to make.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the INDIA bloc's symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the INDIA bloc's symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday, seated in a chair steeped in history. The chair was once used by India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.The information was shared by Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera, who was involved in organising the event at the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at 10, Rajaji Marg in New Delhi.“The chair on which Meira Kumar sat during today's public impeachment proceedings against the CEC was once occupied by the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, the great-grandfather of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi,” Khera later said in a post on X.“It was Nehru Ji's chair throughout his tenure as prime minister. It witnessed some of the most consequential decisions in our nation's history and carries the weight of that legacy,” he added.Khera said that Meira Kumar, sitting in the same chair, pronounced Gyanesh Kumar “unfit to continue as the Chief Election Commissioner of India”.“Gyanesh Kumar has been rejected by the people of India. It is only a matter of time before he goes,” he said.The INDIA bloc organised the symbolic proceedings, accusing the CEC of allegedly facilitating the deletion of voters' names from electoral rolls and demanding that he be tried in court for treason and jailed.Kumar opened the proceedings, saying the opposition had decided to convene the meeting because of alleged wrongful deletions of eligible voters.“When this issue is raised by the INDIA bloc, there is no accountability. So we have decided that the INDIA bloc will hold a meeting and bring a proposal to remove Gyanesh Kumar,” she said.The resolution was moved by Kharge, seconded by Samajwadi Party leader Harendra Malik and supported by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition MPs and civil society representatives. It was adopted unanimously through a show of hands.Kharge alleged that the right to vote was under threat and accused the Election Commission of functioning at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.Rahul Gandhi described the proceedings as a “political weapon” against those who, he alleged, had colluded to destroy people's votes.“I don't think anything like this has ever happened in history,” Gandhi said, adding that “every single institution is closed to us”.“I fully support the motion to impeach Gyanesh Kumar, who should be tried for treason in court and justice should be served,” he said.The BJP criticised the event, accusing the INDIA bloc of making a “mockery” of Parliament and democracy. BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said the opposition was holding a “mock parliament” and took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi.The symbolic proceedings came ahead of the INDIA bloc's November 1 march and rally at Ramlila Maidan, where opposition leaders are seeking to intensify pressure for the CEC's removal and raise concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Texas woman kept emus, ostriches, goats and 30 chickens on her 14-acre homestead, prompting a feud over property rules; the state's Supreme Court has now blocked her neighbours' broad demand to inspect the land
articles.summary: A long-running dispute over animals, fences and property rules on a 14-acre Texas homestead has ended, at least for now, with a win for the landowner.
articles.body: A long-running dispute over animals, fences and property rules on a 14-acre Texas homestead has ended, at least for now, with a win for the landowner. Pamela Bosco, who kept emus, ostriches, goats and about 30 chickens on her Hays County property, faced a broad legal demand from neighbours seeking access to inspect her land. The Texas Supreme Court has now blocked that demand, ruling that the neighbours did not show a clear legal right to enter and inspect the property. The decision, published in the court’s case record for In re Pamela Bosco, narrows how far neighbours can go when they allege violations of private property restrictions, as per Justia U.S. Law:The homestead at the centreBosco’s property was more than a typical residential plot. It was a working homestead of roughly 14 acres, where she raised large flightless birds as well as goats and dozens of chickens. Her neighbours, however, argued that the animals and related activities conflicted with the restrictions governing their subdivision.The disagreement escalated beyond an ordinary neighbourhood complaint. The neighbours sought court-ordered access to Bosco’s land so they could inspect it and gather evidence for their claims. Bosco resisted, arguing that allowing such an inspection would intrude on her property rights without a sufficient legal basis. The dispute eventually reached Texas’s highest civil court.What the neighbours wantedThe core issue was discovery, the legal process by which parties obtain information before a trial. The neighbours wanted an order allowing them to enter Bosco’s property to inspect conditions relevant to their allegations. In effect, they sought a broad right of access to land that Bosco owned and occupied.Bosco asked the Texas Supreme Court to stop that inspection order. Her position was that the neighbours had not established that they were entitled to enter her property, particularly when their underlying claims and the scope of the proposed inspection remained disputed. The court agreed that the demand was too expansive to stand as issued.The Supreme Court’s decisionThe Texas Supreme Court granted Bosco’s request for relief and blocked the neighbours’ broad inspection demand. The court’s reasoning turned on the principle that a party cannot use discovery to obtain access to private property without first showing a proper legal basis for that access.In practical terms, the ruling does not necessarily decide whether Bosco’s animals or homestead activities violate the subdivision’s restrictions. Instead, it decides that the neighbours cannot compel a wide-ranging physical inspection of her land simply by asserting that such an inspection might support their case. They must pursue their claims through the ordinary legal process and meet the required standards before seeking intrusive access.Why the case mattersThe decision is significant for rural and semi-rural landowners across Texas, where homesteads often sit near newer residential developments and where neighbours may disagree about noise, animals, fencing, drainage or the character of a neighbourhood. Property restrictions can be enforceable, but the Texas Supreme Court’s ruling makes clear that enforcing them does not automatically give neighbouring owners a licence to enter someone else’s land.It also highlights the difference between alleging a violation and proving one. A neighbour may believe that emus, ostriches, goats or chickens breach a deed restriction, but the courts require evidence gathered through lawful means. The ruling signals that inspection of private property is an exceptional remedy, not a routine tool for gathering leverage in a neighbourhood dispute.A feud with wider lessonsFor Bosco, the ruling preserves her ability to continue using her homestead while the underlying dispute is resolved through proper legal channels. For her neighbours, it means their case cannot rely on a sweeping inspection order unless they satisfy the court that such access is justified. The Texas Supreme Court’s decision therefore draws a boundary between legitimate enforcement of property restrictions and an overbroad intrusion into private land.The case is also a reminder that rural living can involve legal friction as communities change. A 14-acre property with exotic birds, goats and poultry may be entirely ordinary to one owner and incompatible with another’s expectations. But Texas’s highest court has made clear that resolving those tensions must begin with respect for property rights and adherence to legal procedure, not with unrestricted access to a neighbour’s land.You use AI every day. articles.title: North Korea tests new cluster-bomb warhead under Kim Jong-un's military push
articles.summary: North Korea has carried out another test of a cluster-bomb warhead for tactical ballistic missiles, with plans to make different variants available to
articles.body: North Korea has carried out another test of a cluster-bomb warhead for tactical ballistic missiles, with plans to make different variants available to military units by the end of this year, Yonhap News Agency reported, citing state media.The test was conducted on Saturday by the country's Missile Administration to examine how effectively the warhead could be used in combat and the extent of damage it could inflict, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported.According to KCNA, research institutes under the Missile Administration "confirmed that Standard Type 2 cluster-bomb warhead is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 12 to 13 hectares with its highest-density power,".The Missile Administration's general director said the warheads had been divided into four categories, each designed for a different purpose."Within this year we will enable units to select and use all those types according to operational aims and specific features of targets," the director was quoted as saying.Cluster bombs scatter multiple smaller explosive devices, known as submunitions, over a large area. This allows them to hit several targets in a single strike.South Korea's military said it had tracked the launch, which took place from an area near Chongju in the country's northwest, with the missile heading towards the Yellow Sea."Under close information sharing between South Korea and the United States, (we) tracked relevant activities before North Korea's missile launch and maintained a readiness posture," South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said on Sunday, Yonhap reported.Seoul's military typically issues statements on North Korean ballistic missile launches soon after they are detected.Shin Jong-woo, secretary-general of the Seoul-based Korea Defense and Security Forum, identified the missile as possibly belonging to the Hwasong-11 Ra series.North Korea had announced a similar test in April, when it fired cluster-bomb warheads mounted on a Hwasong-11 Ra tactical ballistic missile. Kim Jong-un and his daughter Ju-ae had watched that launch, Yonhap reported.The latest test comes as the foreign ministers of South Korea, the US and Japan renewed their push for North Korea's complete denuclearisation at a trilateral meeting in Atlanta.Separately, US secretary of state Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Trump was still willing to meet Kim Jong-un, provided Pyongyang was prepared to discuss matters of concern to Washington and its allies.No meeting between the two leaders has been arranged so far, Yonhap reported.You use AI every day.
